diagnostic_evidence.quote: (3) For the fully discrete scheme, we establish stability and derive a convergence estimate.
To simplify the presentation, we will limit ourselves to the case
The case $\alpha\left(t\right)\ne\beta\left(t\right)$ is studied in Section

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and contribution (3) present a convergence estimate for the model with independent orders alpha(t), beta(t). Theorem thm:convergence covers only alpha = beta. The phrase 'to simplify the presentation' suggests the general case is routine, but it is not. With alpha != beta the error inequality involves two different kernels, Delta^alpha||xi_u||^2 + Delta^beta||xi_B||^2, and the single-kernel Gronwall theorem invoked does not apply. The paper gives no argument for this case.

failure_location.quote: which is then applied to the coupled MHD system

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the abstract and contribution claims explicitly to alpha = beta and remove the suggestion that the general case is merely presentational. Alternatively, prove a two-kernel discrete Gronwall estimate.
issues.overall_effect: No convergence guarantee exists for the asymmetric regime alpha != beta, which the model formulation advertises and the numerical experiments study.
issues.title: Convergence advertised for the coupled variable-order system but proved only for alpha = beta
issues.why_classification: The repair either withdraws an advertised part of the scope or requires a new nontrivial Gronwall argument. The alpha = beta result itself survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which provides a suitable estimate even when the fractional order

issues.failure_explanation: The left-hand side is E = Theta - R. R accumulates positive parts (delta_{j,k})_+ = (b_{j,k+1} - b_{j-1,k})_+ over all levels without cancellation. For a non-monotone order these terms add up on every increase of nu, and the factor tau^{1-nu_j} can change markedly between levels. The coefficient of ||phi^k||^2 in R can therefore exceed b_{n,k} in Theta, making E_n negative. No lower bound E_n >= c||phi^n||^2 (or nonnegativity) is proved. The inequality is valid but bounds nothing about ||u_h^n|| or ||B_h^n||, contrary to its 'Stability' title and to the claim that it works for non-monotone nu.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a coercivity bound for E_n via a Gronwall argument controlling R under a bounded-variation or Lipschitz condition on nu. Alternatively, for alpha = beta, combine Lemma lem:frac1 with the discrete fractional Gronwall theorem (lambda = 0) to bound ||u_h^n||^2 + ||B_h^n||^2 directly.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised unconditional stability of the fully discrete scheme, especially for non-monotone orders, is not established.
issues.title: Stability estimate controls an indefinite corrected functional, so no bound on the discrete solution follows
issues.why_classification: A contained new argument using tools already in the paper, possibly with an extra condition on nu, restores a comparable stability result. No new global architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses ||r_1^n||, ||r_2^n|| <= C tau uniformly in n. The L1 truncation error is an integral of u'(s) - (u^k - u^{k-1})/tau against the kernel. An O(tau) bound needs control of the second time derivative, for example u_tt bounded. Assumption assu:regularity provides only partial_t u in L^infty, which yields an O(1) bound, so the time rate is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add partial_tt u, partial_tt B in L^infty(0,T;L^2) to Assumption assu:regularity and include the standard frozen-order L1 truncation estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The first-order temporal rate in Theorem thm:convergence rests on an unstated regularity hypothesis.
issues.title: O(tau) truncation bound for L1 operator not implied by the stated regularity
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard smoothness hypothesis, which the manufactured solutions satisfy, and a routine estimate preserves the stated rate and method.

issues.failure_explanation: The projector gives (grad psi_u, grad v_h) = (psi_p, div v_h). The error equation, however, contains (1/Re)(grad psi_u, grad xi_u) - (psi_p, div xi_u) = (1/Re - 1)(psi_p, div xi_u), which vanishes only if Re = 1. This term is silently dropped in (eq:conv_step2). Bounding it needs a pressure approximation estimate ||psi_p|| <= C h^l ||p||_{H^l}, and no pressure regularity is assumed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the Stokes projector with the 1/Re factor, or bound the extra term by ||psi_p|| ||grad xi_u|| after adding p in L^infty(0,T;H^l) to the assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The error equation behind Theorem thm:convergence is incomplete for Re != 1, which includes the regimes used in the experiments (Re = 200, 300).
issues.title: Stokes projector lacks the 1/Re scaling, leaving an omitted pressure-projection term in the error equation
issues.why_classification: This is a local fix with a standard estimate, and the h^{min(l,m)} + tau rate is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (eq:elliptic) is the weak form of -Delta phi = div B~. Hence div(B~ - grad phi) = div B~ - Delta phi = 2 div B~. Weakly, (div B_h, psi_h) = (div B~, psi_h) + (grad phi_h, grad psi_h) = 2(div B~, psi_h). The stated procedure therefore amplifies the divergence instead of removing it, contradicting its stated purpose and the reported reductions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of the right-hand side of (eq:elliptic), or set B_h^n = B~_h^n + grad phi_h^n.
issues.overall_effect: The specified cleaning procedure does not deliver its guarantee, so the reported post-cleaning divergence values cannot come from the algorithm as written.
issues.title: Divergence-cleaning step as written doubles the divergence
issues.why_classification: A one-sign correction restores the intended projection, with no change to the method or results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the Dirichlet values are imposed again before proceeding to the next time level
This behavior agrees well with the theoretical prediction obtained in Theorem

issues.failure_explanation: The cleaned B_h^n replaces the solution of Problem prob:fully and enters the memory sums at all later levels. However, grad phi_h of a continuous finite element function is generally discontinuous, so B_h^n is not in C_h, which is a subset of H^1. This violates the premise of Problem prob:fully that B_h^i lies in C_h. Psi_h is also defined as an infinite-dimensional subspace of H^1, so the discrete problem is not well specified. Re-imposing Dirichlet values afterwards is a further unanalyzed modification. Theorems thm:stability and thm:convergence therefore do not apply to the computed scheme, yet the numerical rates are presented as confirming Theorem thm:convergence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use cleaning only as post-processing that is not fed back into the time stepping, or project grad phi_h onto C_h and analyze the modified update. Specify Psi_h as a finite element space, and rerun or reinterpret the verification tests accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The link between the analysis and all reported computations is broken. The convergence tests do not verify the analyzed scheme, and the implemented method has no proven stability or convergence.
issues.title: Implemented scheme with cleaning differs from the analyzed scheme and leaves the conforming space
issues.why_classification: The repair requires either re-running the experiments with the analyzed scheme or extending the analysis to a modified update. This is contained work but more than a local edit, and the main theory survives.
